option_relations.rationale: Crescentic IgA nephropathy (rapidly progressive IgA glomerulonephritis) is a specific presentation of IgA Nephropathy, making it an equivalent diagnosis in this context.

Lupus nephritis is a distinct disease from IgA nephropathy, although both can cause glomerulonephritis. The presence of IgA deposition and anti-SM/U1-NRNP antibodies does not automatically equate to Lupus nephritis class IV.

Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) is a systemic autoimmune disease that can cause various organ manifestations, including nephritis. While the patient has positive ANA, anti-SM, and U1-NRNP, the primary kidney biopsy findings point strongly to IgA nephropathy rather than SLE with IgA nephropathy as a co-occurrence.
IgA nephropathy with crescentic transformation describes a specific form of IgA nephropathy, making it an equivalent diagnosis to the broader IgA Nephropathy leaf.
